PROBLEM (verified): RuntimeEngine.turn (engine.py ~191) loops TURN_NARRATION_ATTEMPTS = 2 times. Each attempt calls the provider, and the CloudflareTurnProvider._dispatch (cloudflare.py ~1149-1230) can itself send up to two HTTP inference requests via _request_allowing_one_transient_retry, then a recovery request (JSON-mode fallback or _recover_malformed_response, each also with a transient retry), plus truncation salvage. The guard retry in the engine (after narration_validator.validate raises ProposalValidationError) therefore multiplies with provider recovery: worst case is roughly eight HTTP requests for one player turn. The contributor guide caps a normal turn at ONE inference request plus ONE shared recovery request (so 2 requests total), and exhaustion must fail closed with a typed error and the state restored.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR (decided by the project owner):
1. One per-turn request budget of 2 inference requests, counted at the single place where the provider sends an inference HTTP request (every send, including a transient retry, a JSON-mode fallback, a malformed-reply recovery and the engine's guard-retry re-ask). The budget resets at the start of each engine turn (explicit call, not hidden state). The first request is free; any second request is "the recovery". When the budget is spent and another request would be needed, raise the existing typed NarrationProviderError (fail closed, state restored exactly as today); never fabricate success. Truncation salvage that needs no new request does not spend budget.
2. The engine's guard retry (validator rejection -> ask again) must respect the same budget: it may re-ask only if budget remains. If the first attempt already spent its recovery, the guard rejection fails the turn closed (re-raise the original ProposalValidationError) with state restored. Keep `guard_retry_used` and `recovery_used` telemetry semantics unchanged.
3. Sanitize the retry feedback. Provider.note_rejection(message) currently puts the full rejection message into the next system prompt (cloudflare.py ~300-310), and that message can name the protected term. Replace it so the narrator is told only a generic reason chosen from the ProposalValidationError.code (or exception class), never the message text, never the term. Write the sentences at 12th-grade level, plain words, one idea per sentence, following docs/narrator-writing-guide.md, e.g. for a knowledge/unavailable-entity leak: "Your last reply named something the player has not met yet. Write this turn again. Describe only what the player can see now." Provide a generic default for any other code. Change the signature to note_rejection(code: str | None) (or similar) so the text cannot be passed through by accident; update callers.
4. Replace `isinstance(self.provider, CloudflareTurnProvider)` and `getattr(self.provider, "note_rejection", None)` in engine.py (~198 and ~230) with an explicit typing.Protocol for the optional provider capabilities (authored_handoff_id, note_rejection, begin_turn / request budget). Providers that lack them (test fakes, other adapters) must still work: give the Protocol-adjacent code a clear default (for example a small base class with no-op methods or an explicit `supports_*` check) rather than getattr. Shared runtime must stay story-agnostic.
5. Do not change what the narrator sees in its normal prompt, validation rules, or any story data.
